extracted.intended_audience: learned natural philosophers, Royal Society members, mathematicians and early modern scientists
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and practical guidance for assessing and producing early modern natural history reports, medical/chemical letters, and mathematical demonstrations (as in Philosophical Transactions). Emphasizes observation, citation of authorities, specimen exchange, mathematical proof, and stepwise practical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical observation and repeated trials
rubrics_metrics.description: ‚I set myself to watch this difference of the time of the tides, and to find out some rule… and I found by many trials…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect repeated observations and experiments to derive rules or hypotheses (e.g., watching tides over many trials to infer a proportional rule). Emphasises careful, repeated measurement rather than reliance on rough or single estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite and weigh testimony of credible authors
rubrics_metrics.description: It is expressly affirmed by authors of good credit… See Latham's Synopsis…; See Brown's Jamaica…; See Catesby's Carolina…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims by referencing established, credible authorities and prior works; use literature to corroborate field reports and identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and examination of specimens for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: To send over some of the skins of those huge lizards… To send over a land-pike…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, provide physical specimens (skins, animals, samples) so others can verify identifications and properties; practical requests for specimens are a standard part of verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for preservation and handling artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The colibris… are not naturally impregnated with the musky odour here mentioned, and it may rather be supposed that the specimens are sometimes perfumed in order to preserve them when sent over in a dried state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret observations of preserved specimens cautiously—preservation methods, long keeping, or treatment can introduce artefacts (odours, colours, textures) that do not reflect the living organism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism and qualification of extravagant reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Though the accounts of its malignant properties may be here somewhat exaggerated… this is a groundless idea… it surely deserves no answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat extraordinary or implausible claims with scepticism; indicate when reports seem exaggerated or without sufficient evidence and avoid answering frivolous or impossible parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of experiments to test medical/chemical hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: He made some experiments on blood, the serum of which he found to be coagulable by a gentle heat and by acids… He hopes of finding out a liquor, which, when injected into the bladder, may dissolve calculi without irritating the bladder itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose and carry out controlled experiments for physiological/chemical claims; report observed effects (e.g., coagulation with heat/acids), practical remedies tried, and their outcomes, and call for further experimental inquiry where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit description of instruments and experimental methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The book contains these particulars:—1. An application of the instruments employed in these experiments. — 2. Experiment belonging to the natural pressure of the air. — …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the apparatus and experimental procedures used so others can understand and reproduce the work; include lists of instruments and what each experiment addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical rigor: clear hypotheses, demonstrations, and numerical bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: This tract… receives the character of being very ingeniously and very mathematically written… by which he teaches a method of squaring the circle, ellipsis, and hyperbola, by an infinite series… calculate the true dimensions as near as you please.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mathematical contributions provide explicit assumptions, stepwise demonstrations/proofs, series or formulae, and numerical approximations or bounds showing convergence and precision (e.g., giving upper and lower bounds for integral/area values). Peer scrutiny by other skilled mathematicians is noted as part of validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine multiple causal factors and account for local variation
rubrics_metrics.description: My Hypothesis for Tides I cast the annual high tides not on the two equinoxes… but as proceeding from a complication of those two causes… The reasons of these varieties are to be attributed to the particular position of those parts, rather than to the general hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing hypotheses (e.g., for tides), account for multiple interacting causes and explain local deviations from general patterns; distinguish between general mechanism and local modifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical, stepwise procedures for prediction or application
rubrics_metrics.description: First, Divide a circle into 12 equal parts… 2d. Let the diameter of the circle be divided into 90 parts or minutes… 3d. Make perpendicular lines… then the proportional minutes cut thereby, will show how many hours or minutes are to be subtracted…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give clear, algorithmic instructions usable by practitioners (e.g., sailors) to implement findings — concrete step-by-step rules, worked examples, and how to apply them to particular places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of taxonomic identification and technical nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Sapindus Saponaria, Lin.; Rhizophora mangle, Lin.; latropha manihot, Lin.; columba leucocephala, Lin.; pellecanus aquilus, Lin.; pulex penetrans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify species using accepted taxonomic names and classifications to reduce ambiguity and facilitate comparison with other authors' observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limits and call for further investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: He hopes this subject will be more thoroughly investigated by some ingenious person in England; so that the gout may cease to be acknowledged even by physicians themselves to be an incurable affection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly note open questions, uncertainties, or incomplete evidence and request further targeted study or experiments from specialists.
